request.summary: Create an interactive Veszprem downtown wayfinding kiosk from the supplied structured SVG map and a separate editable destination table.
request.audience: Visitors choosing a downtown landmark on a landscape touch display in Veszprem.
request.primaryGoal: Let a visitor find a named destination, draw a real route through the SVG point graph, and understand approximate distance without rebuilding the app when labels change.

assumptions: The supplied 1341x947 SVG is the authoritative map geometry and contains 35 location shapes, 35 location points, and 625 route points.
The destination table owns public labels and descriptions; SVG ids remain the stable routing keys.
Heroes' Gate is the representative kiosk start and can be changed to another valid SVG location id.
Veszprem Arena and the sports swimming pool appear in the map legend but sit outside the supplied downtown route graph, so they are explicitly marked off-map.
The package contains public landmark names and synthetic descriptive metadata only; it contains no customer or personal data.

surfaceStrategy.rationale: The interaction is designed for 16:9 landscape kiosks at 1920x1080 and 1366x768; unsupported narrow and portrait zones should use a dedicated composition.

ownership.rationale: Operators quick-edit destination names, categories, descriptions, accessibility, and route availability without changing code.
The kiosk label, origin, reset timing, and map calibration belong to the installed instance.
Coordinated presets are safe defaults while Custom exposes one flat semantic palette compatible with the editor.
Search and route selection exist only for the current visitor session.
Graph construction and route semantics follow the proven Wallboard map implementation and are not operator-authored content.

views.purpose: Search or browse landmarks while the complete reference map remains visible.
Show the selected landmark, route line, approximate distance, walking time, and off-map state.

inputs.action: Select a destination from the directory or directly from its map shape.

session.expectation: An active route clears after the configured timeout; Clear route returns immediately to the complete destination list.

rendering.rationale: The map and directory preserve their landscape split while header, panel, and list density reallocate between the two bounded surfaces.

motion.rationale: Only the route stroke reveals progressively; directory and map remain stable for orientation.

media.fallback: Keep the destination directory available and show no route if the packaged SVG cannot mount.
media.rationale: The supplied SVG contains both the reference artwork and the location and route geometry required by the experience.

branding.provenance: The Veszprem identity and map artwork come from the user-supplied veszprem-belvaros-wayfinding.svg reference.
branding.fallback: Preserve the reference artwork; operators may edit only the shell title and semantic palette.

settings.purpose: Short instruction above the destination directory.
SVG and table id used as the kiosk's route origin.
Message shown for a bound but empty destination table.
Seconds before the selected route clears.
Maximum SVG distance used to connect neighboring route points.
SVG pixels per displayed metre for approximate route detail.
Selects the coordinated Light, Dark, or Custom shell palette.

dynamicText.fallback: Reduce to the near-viewing floor, then preserve one line and ellipsize only the tail.
dynamicText.rationale: A custom kiosk title must coexist with identity and current-location context in the bounded header.

dynamicText.fallback: Keep the leading destination name and English label on separate stable rows; ellipsize only their tails.
dynamicText.rationale: A scrollable touch directory needs stable row height while preserving recognizable prefixes.

dynamicText.fallback: Wrap the selected destination to three lines before reducing description or route-detail density.
dynamicText.rationale: The selected landmark is the route view's primary instruction and must remain complete.

states.expectation: The complete supplied map and unbound representative destination table fill the primary kiosk.
The dark shell preserves near-viewing text and touch targets around the unchanged reference map.
A connected landmark draws an animated route and displays approximate distance and walking time.
An off-map venue remains discoverable but never receives an invented route.
Every flat custom color control applies to the shell and route semantics.
A long operator title remains bounded beside the reference identity and current location.
Long bilingual destination labels preserve stable touch rows.
The full selected destination wraps without colliding with route details or actions.
A bound empty destination table stays empty and shows the configured state.
Processed TABLE row arrays normalize to the same destination model.
Quick-edited destination labels update without rebuilding the app.

behaviors.expectation: Route and location points build the same proximity graph rule as the production map app and Dijkstra selects the shortest connected path.
Map-shape taps and directory buttons drive the same selected destination and route rendering.
Destinations outside the supplied downtown route graph remain labeled as off-map without fabricated geometry.
The configured timeout removes route geometry and restores the complete destination list.
Destination table updates replace visible labels in place.

visualDirection.summary: Keep the supplied illustrated Veszprem map dominant and add a restrained visitor-centre interaction shell rather than restyling it as a generic dashboard.
signatureChoices: The full bilingual illustrated map remains visible while the right rail acts as a focused touchscreen directory.
A red route line animates directly through the map's own route points and preserves its warm civic palette.
avoid: Inventing routes to disconnected external venues

visualReview.intent: A credible visitor-centre kiosk where the reference map remains the hero and route selection is obvious, readable, and reversible.
focus: Verify the complete SVG remains sharp and uncropped at both bounded surfaces.
Verify destination rows, selected names, route summaries, and descenders remain readable without overlap.
Verify map and list taps select the same landmark and route animation never obscures the underlying map.
Verify Light, Dark, and Custom shells remain coordinated with the fixed reference artwork.
